thread:
sam: Hey team — new user hit a weird failure on Windows + WSL quickstart. First call returns a TLS handshake error from our SDK, then a 403 when they retry from WSL.
liz: Ugh. Any repro steps? OS + Node/Python? :thinking_face:
sam: Windows 11, WSL2 Ubuntu, node 20. Tried both node SDK and curl from inside WSL. curl -> handshake error; node -> threw 'UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE' then after setting NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 it got 403.
ankit: That TLS error usually means the container (WSL) is missing CA bundles or there's a proxy rewriting certs. Are they behind a corp SSL proxy?
sam: They said company laptop with an endpoint agent. But they also tried on home machine (clean) and got same 403 after quickstart. They opened the workspace and billing shows active. No card required.
ben: Could be our billing gating returning 403 for firstcall if workspace created via SSO and no org-level billing configured. Do we have logs for their user id?
support-bot: (automated) Requested logs: trace_id=tr_XYZ123 -> 403: billing_required false; reason=policy_restricted
liz: Wait billing_required false but still 403 + reason policy_restricted? That's inconsistent.
manually: (note: manual annotation) Often when org is created via invite flow the workspace owner role isn't set, causing auth path to fall back to a restricted policy.
maya: I can repro locally by creating a fresh workspace via invite link — first API key works but returns 403 until I finish the workspace billing wizard in the console. Might be a UX gap.
sam: The user reported they never saw the billing wizard. They signed up via SSO invite. No redirect to billing.
ankit: Two things to check: 1) SDK retry behavior when TLS fails — we should not flip to retry path that tries different auth header. 2) Server-side: why are we returning policy_restricted if billing_required is false.
ben: I'll pull the policy logs. Can someone DM the user's email? Need trace_id + user id.
sam: Sent DM with trace_id and user email.
ben: Looking at logs: user has license=trial, org has payment_metadata=null, policy engine flagged 'needs_org_admin' for API access. So server responds 403 with code POLICY_RESTRICTED even though billing_required flag is false. Bug in the policy inference.
liz: Actionable: 1) devex: update quickstart docs to call out SSO/invite path and show the console flow to complete workspace billing. 2) infra: patch policy engine to set clearer code and surface a link in error response. 3) sdk: don't switch auth behavior on TLS errors — surface original error and add clearer retry guidance.
ankit: I'll open infra issue and post back. ben, can you craft a temporary support message we can paste for users hit by this? Something like: "If you signed up through an invite/SSO, go to Console > Billing to finish org setup; if you still get 403 contact support with trace_id X".
ben: Draft: "Hi — thanks for the report. If you joined via SSO or invite please complete your org setup in the Console (Workspace > Billing). If you've completed that and still see 403, please reply with trace_id=tr_XYZ123 and we'll escalate." Feel free to shorten.
sam: OK I'll send that.
liz: Also filing a doc PR: quickstart.md add a note under "First call" about SSO/invite edge case and a troubleshooting snippet for WSL + proxy certs:

```
# Troubleshoot WSL certs
# in WSL: sudo apt-get install ca-certificates
# verify: curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
```

ankit: Nice. I'll track infra ticket -> POLICY-1423. Assign to @ben for error string change.
ben: Assigned. Will update here when done. :thumbsup:
sam: Thanks all, sending the support reply now. Will follow up if user still blocked.
maya: FYI I hit same flow in a different org earlier this week. Happy to help validate a fix.
support-bot: (automated) Ticket created: SUPPORT-8891 referencing trace_id=tr_XYZ123 and POLICY-1423.
